stem.text: Show that, at the point (–1, –2) on C, dy/dx = 8/11.

points.text: 5(1–y′) – (1/2)y′ – 1 = 0 ⇒ y′ = 8/11; substitutes (–1,–2) into 5(x–y)⁴(1–y′)+y′y⁻¹+x⁻¹=0, AG, CWO. Might see y′(y⁻¹–5(x–y)⁴) = –5(x–y)⁴–x⁻¹

explanation.text: Both terms on the left need implicit differentiation: (x–y)⁵ via the chain rule (treating y as a function of x, so d/dx(x–y) = 1–y′), and ln(xy) via the chain rule plus the product rule inside the log, or equivalently by splitting ln(xy) = lnx + lny first (often simpler).

reasoningChain: Differentiate (x–y)⁵ using the chain rule: 5(x–y)⁴ · d/dx(x–y) = 5(x–y)⁴(1–y′).
Differentiate ln(xy): either split as lnx+lny (giving 1/x + y′/y) or use the chain rule on the product xy directly — both give the same result.
The RHS (1+ln2) is constant, so its derivative is 0.
Substitute x=–1, y=–2 into the differentiated equation and solve the resulting linear equation for y′.

inferredMistakes.text: Forgetting the extra factor of (1–y′) when differentiating (x–y)⁵, i.e. writing 5(x–y)⁴ as if x–y were just x, missing that y depends on x.
Treating ln(xy) as ln(x)·ln(y) rather than ln(x)+ln(y), which gives a completely different (and wrong) derivative.

stem.text: Find the value of d2y/dx2 at the point (–1, –2).

points.text: –(y′)2y–2 + y–1y″ – x–2 = 0; differentiates y′y⁻¹+x⁻¹. Might see (xy′+y)/xy differentiated using product or quotient rules, e.g. [xy(xy″+2y′) – (xy′+y)2]/(xy)2, or –(xy)–2(xy′+y)2 + (xy)–1(xy″+2y′)

markScheme.note: MS gives two further alternative methods for this part (differentiating the rearranged y′ expression directly, or a quotient-rule variant); all three reach y″ = 86/1331 and are worth the full 5 marks. Only the method starting from part (a)'s equation is transcribed here.

explanation.text: Differentiate the whole equation from part (a) — 5(x–y)⁴(1–y′) + y′y⁻¹ + x⁻¹ = 0 — a second time with respect to x. The first term needs the product rule (since both (x–y)⁴ and (1–y′) depend on x) plus the chain rule on (x–y)⁴; the second term y′y⁻¹ also needs the product rule since both factors depend on x.

reasoningChain: Start from the differentiated equation in part (a): 5(x–y)⁴(1–y′) + y′y⁻¹ + x⁻¹ = 0.
Differentiate 5(x–y)⁴(1–y′) using the product rule: the derivative of (x–y)⁴ brings in another factor of (1–y′), and the derivative of (1–y′) brings in –y″.
Differentiate y′y⁻¹ using the product rule: this brings in y″y⁻¹ and a term in (y′)²y⁻².
Substitute x=–1, y=–2, y′=8/11 (from part (a)) into the resulting equation and solve for y″.

inferredMistakes.text: Forgetting that y′ itself depends on x when differentiating (1–y′) a second time, treating it as a constant and losing the –y″ term from that factor.
Not substituting the value of y′ found in part (a) before solving for y″, leaving two unknowns in one equation.
